correctness.rationale: Pinned theorem treats 3-vertex path L=[[1,-1,0],[-1,2,-1],[0,-1,1]], h>m>ell>0, linear H_r=diag(r)-dL for every finite d>0; Perron max eigenvalue is simple, decreases strictly with d, lies strictly between the mean and h. Independently expanded tridiagonal F_{a,b,c}=det(zI-H) and verified F_{a,b,c}-F_{a,c,b}=d(z-a)(b-c) and F_{a,b,c}(a)=d[(a-b)(a-c)+d(2a-b-c)]. A tie between reflected placements requires eigenvalue equal the shared endpoint rate. Small-d first/second perturbations select medium-center as unique optimum; absence of admissible Perron ties proves its global superiority. The two nonoptimal layouts with common m endpoint meet only if 2m>h+ell and then at exact d*=(h-m)(m-ell)/(2m-h-ell), common principal eigenvalue m and opposite derivative signs; when 2m<=h+ell they never meet. Transversality verified by nonzero derivative of common characteristic determinant; n=1,2 or triangle permutation symmetry rules out smaller reversal. Independent exact characteristic calculation and spectral numerics for (h,m,ell)=(6,5,1) verified d*=4/3, and opposite orders d=1 vs 2. The parameter-uniform proof is analytic.
residual_risks: Only h>m>ell>0, d>0, linear three-site path, symmetric nearest-neighbor dispersal; no larger graphs.

value.rationale: Exactly classifying the three distinct-rate placements of a canonical minimal connected habitat path explains a sharply located dispersal-driven ranking reversal and rules out any smaller connected unweighted network. The crossing layouts are globally nonoptimal without further constraints, but under realistic fixed-endpoint placement they become the two relevant choices; this motivation is explicit and mathematically substantive despite the three-vertex setting.
residual_risks: The reversing placements are not globally optimal among three unconstrained permutations; decision significance requires fixing an endpoint or similar spatial constraint.
Only linear, three-site symmetric uniform dispersal; no nonlinear growth or epidemiological inference.

limitations: Only h>m>ell>0, d>0, linear three-site path, symmetric nearest-neighbor dispersal; no larger graphs.
